moments.name: 18…Rxg5
moments.headline: 18…Rxg5!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Puts the rook on g5 where it can be taken.
White can take, but after 19.Qxg5+ Kh7 20.Qh4+ Kg7 the engine rates it 0.00.
White was threatening Bxf6, winning the queen. Rxg5 takes care of it.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 18…Rxg5!! gives up the rook on g5 to stay in the game: after it Black holds the balance (0.00); anything else leaves Black losing (+4.90).

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 18…Rxg5 puts the rook on g5 where it can be taken by the queen on h4. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It takes the bishop on g5.

why.title: If White takes the rook
why.text: 19.Qxg5+ is met by 19…Kh7, preparing …Nd5 and …Kg7. Then 20…Nd5 uncovers an attack on the queen on g5, and 23…Qf6 attacks the b2 pawn, which is undefended. Black is a piece down: Black holds the balance (0.00). This is White's best try.

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 18…Re6, is clearly weaker (+4.90 against 0.00). White answers 19.Rae1, threatening Rxe6, winning the queen. That would leave Black losing.
